body:
> **This does not fix the aliasing in #461.** It fixes the misleading warning beside it. The corruption is untouched and #461 stays open — see the last section.

## The warning was wrong

Under `--memory shared --address-rebase`, meld named a component as carrying **no** relocation metadata when its only substantive module was fully reloc-covered, and told the user to rebuild with `--emit-relocs` when they already had.

Reported by @cpetig with a complete reproduction. The cause, confirmed on their inputs:

```rust
component.core_modules.iter()
    .any(|module| !reloc::has_reloc_metadata(&module.custom_sections))
```

`any(!has_reloc)` over **all** core modules. A component whose imports pass records by pointer gets three core modules from wit-component — the real one, a lowered-import shim, and a fixup — and the latter two carry no relocs by construction. So one **281-byte shim** tainted a **16109-byte** module holding `linking`, `reloc.CODE` and `reloc.DATA`.

## The fix asks a narrower question

Does this module's *missing* reloc metadata actually put the artifact at risk? True only when the module **both defines its own memory and lacks relocs** — because `compute_shared_memory_plan` populates `bases` from exactly that "defines a memory" test, so a module without one provably gets base 0 and cannot be shifted into a neighbour's window.

Measured on the reporter's inputs, split's three modules are:

| module | memory | code | reloc |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (real, 16109 B) | yes | yes | **yes** |
| 1 (shim, 281 B) | no | yes | no |
| 2 (fixup, 133 B) | no | no | no |

Verified end to end: the false warning is gone — 0 occurrences of "NO relocation metadata", down from one naming split.

## The control, and a correction to my first attempt at one

My first control fused two components I assumed lacked relocs. The warning didn't fire, which looked like a pass. Checking them showed **both have relocs** — there was nothing to warn about, so the control proved nothing.

A valid control is `falcon-cascade-stream-composed-v1.138.wasm`, whose memory-defining module genuinely has none. With it the warning still fires **and** path-F still hard-fails with `MissingRelocMetadata`, so the check keeps its teeth for the case it exists for.

Three unit tests pin the predicate on the shapes that actually occur. **Potency measured:** restoring the old `any(!has_reloc)` semantics fails exactly the shim-taint test while the memory-defining-no-reloc control still passes — so the pair discriminates rather than passing either way.

## A false statement about a safety gate, removed

The comment beside this warning claimed the dangerous case "is already a hard error there (path-F)". The reproduction disproves it: path-F fires only when a module has **no** relocs at all. Worth removing even while the gate's gap stays open.

## What is still broken

Re-run on the reporter's inputs **after** this change:

```
load/store offsets   64K–128K = 196    128K and above = 0
```

with split placed at base 131072. Unchanged.

The investigation did move the diagnosis, though. Split's rebase plan **is** built (`code_offsets=101`, base `0x20000`) and **is** applied — 109 reloc sites matched during the rewrite, and its `i32.const` addresses are correctly rebased (119 values above 128K in the output). Only absolute addresses folded into memarg `offset=` fields are left alone, of which its input has 95.

So a module *with* relocs is trusted to have them for every absolute address it holds, and #461 is where that trust fails. A hypothesis I tested and discarded: the handle-table re-rewrite in `merger/mod.rs`, which rebuilds bodies with `address_rebasing=false` and overwrites `mf.body`. It fits the symptoms but never fires for these inputs.

```
fmt 0 · clippy 0 · clippy --all-features 0
test --workspace 0 (921 passed) · --all-features 0 (920 passed)
traceability ratchet 0 new
```
